spec.title: codkit PROP-009: The upgrade-cycle orchestrator - state, journal, phases, cadence

facts.WEEKLY-CADENCE: **We track the release tags of upstream, at a weekly step** (fact: the tags `1.128`…`1.135` come about a week apart; the window `1.134→1.135` is 267 commits). The pin moves only on green CI; a stuck cycle blocks nobody - we stay on the old pin and release from it.
facts.BATCHING-IS-EXCEPTION: Batching several tags is allowed as an exception (a toolchain cascade, for instance), but not as the norm: on large diffs automatic rename detection degrades.
facts.DAILY-FORECAST: **A daily forecast** (independent of tags): a nightly dry run of applying the delta to a fresh upstream `main`; a report by owners - «intervention X, the upstream cause commit Y will break it soon». It changes nothing; it is implemented by the same apply engine in dry-run mode.
facts.OUR-RELEASE-RHYTHM: **Our release is a separate rhythm**: we release when the product is ready, from the current green pin; the product version is its own, and the upstream pin is a machine field in the publication artifact.

p.cycle-state-role: Committed on the cycle branch; the presence of the file in the patch-set work tree means «a cycle is running»; the state is written atomically (a temporary file + rename) after every change.

tr.td: 2 for legacy tagged pins, 3 for revision/resolution evidence, 4 when explicit branch-transition authorization is recorded; schemas 2 and 3 remain readable and retain their serialization
the source and the target pin

the name of the cycle branch in the patch set: `<cycleBranchPrefix><targetTag>` (`codkit/cycle/<targetTag>` by default); the schema checks Git ref safety, exact equality with the config is the engine's job
a human-readable «what next» hint (printed by `cycle status`)

durable recovery identity: init keeps the base commit/branch from before the first mutation; restart keeps the bump/base commits from before the reset. An exact partial state either continues deterministically or is refused loudly
the classification: the key is the outcome (`clean`,`shifted`,`merged`,`conflict`,`target-deleted`,`target-renamed`,`rule-broken`,`contract-failed`), the value is an array of artifact paths
the artifacts already resolved after a stop

p.CYCLE-CONTROL-RECORD: Before `reset --hard`, `restart` atomically duplicates the recovery snapshot into the local `.codkit/cycle-control.json` (`codkitCycleControl: 1`, `status: running|done`). This file is not committed and lies outside the reset scope: if the tracked `cycle/state.json` disappeared after the reset, a repeated `restart` and `status` finish the operation from the exact bump/base SHAs. `done` is kept until the next verified start, so that a crash after the last mutation has an idempotent answer.

facts.JOURNAL-FILES: `cycle/log/<targetTag>.md` (human-readable, committed) and `cycle/log/<targetTag>.jsonl` (machine-readable, one atomically appended line per event: `{"codkitCycleJournal":1,"ts":…,"artifact":…,"outcome":…,"resolution":…,"cause":…,"by":"human|agent:<name>","verified":…}`).
facts.JOURNAL-COMPLETENESS: The completeness check: every artifact with a non-`clean` outcome has a record in the jsonl - otherwise `cycle continue` does not let the cycle into the `done` phase (exit 1, `CK-E-LOG-INCOMPLETE`).
facts.JOURNAL-AGENT-ENTRIES: The journal of agent decisions is the same jsonl with the field `by: "agent:<name>"`; an agent writes there through an ordinary file (the contract for the agent protocol FEAT-004).

phases.title: 4. The state machine - phases and transitions

p.CYCLE-BRANCH-TRANSITION: By default the target must descend from the source pin. An operator may explicitly select `cycle start <target> --allow-branch-transition` for sibling release branches: both pins must descend from the configured upstream anchor, remain different, and the target must not be an ancestor of the source. Init records the exact authorized anchor as `branchTransitionAnchor` in state schema 4 before mutation. Recovery consumes that recorded authorization and refuses a changed configured anchor; legacy schemas cannot carry the field. This preserves the official release commit as the target rather than inventing a merge commit solely to satisfy ancestry.

p.PHASES-RESUMABLE: Every phase is idempotent and resumable: `continue` re-reads `state.json`, validates the actual state of the tree and of the patch set and continues from `phase`; an interruption at any point loses no data.

facts.PHASE-INIT: **init** (`cycle start <target>`): the checks (PROP-007 §14) → the branch `codkit/cycle/<targetTag>` off the current main → the canonical pin commit (an edit of `codkit.json`: pin.tag/sha/date; message `codkit cycle: bump pin to <tag>`) → state → phase=apply.
facts.PHASE-APPLY: **apply**: the rename step (PROP-008 §6) → carrying the artifacts over the renames in a separate canonical commit → the classification loop (PROP-008 §5) over every artifact against the new pin → filling in `state.artifacts` → the `clean|shifted|merged` artifacts are regenerated automatically (PROP-004 §5 against the new pin; the `pin` field of the headers is updated) and committed as one machine canonical «regeneration» commit (the «regenerable» category: it may be thrown away and created anew) → if `conflict|target-deleted|rule-broken` are empty, phase=deps-advisory, otherwise phase=resolve and a **stop** (exit 3): the red list is printed, grouped by cause commits, with the owners from the inventory.
facts.PHASE-RESOLVE: **resolve** (humans and agents work in the tree; the conflicts are materialized with the standard markers): after the edits, `cycle continue` runs `save` over the affected files; every resolution is a separate commit with the trailer `Cause: <sha>` (prepared by the hook of PROP-007 §19); a journal record is mandatory; once all are resolved → phase=deps-advisory.
facts.PHASE-DEPS-ADVISORY: **deps-advisory**: the semantic readers the project type declares are run over the `oldPin..newPin` diff (the readers are the type's answer, not the engine's; VS Code type: `spec://codkit/modules/vscode/PROP-005#VSCODE-ADVISORY-READERS`) → a report on «what changed in the toolchain»; a non-empty report in interactive mode is a **stop point** (exit 3; a human runs `npm install` in the tree by the protocol - the daemons are stopped beforehand with `build down --all`); under `--ci` the report goes to the log and the cycle continues.
facts.PHASE-STABILIZE: **stabilize**: the pass opens by bringing the tree back to the development mode - the fresh load the operator would run, without the generated branch and from the pinned inputs - because the build profile of the previous pass leaves the tree in the generated mode, own code and inputs committed on the branch, and the verify of the pass judges the delta as the operator's verify does (PROP-005 `##OWN-EXCLUDED-LOCALLY`): over a tree left in the generated mode it read as one `UNTRACKED-INTERVENTION` per own file, and every second pass was red; then `build up` → `build errors` (the full output) → own tests → contract tests → (by profile) upstream tests → marking the `contract-failed` artifacts - every artifact of the inventory whose contract test failed, the records the classification never saw included (the own manifest of a failed own unit, a service-override, a removed record), since resolve describes a `contract-failed` artifact from the inventory and not from the classification → red → phase=resolve (back); green → phase=done.
facts.PHASE-DONE: **done** (`continue`): the journal completeness check → a snapshot of the inventory metrics into the cycle journal → a commit of the journal and of the state (the runtime state is deleted by the final commit) → the instruction to merge the cycle branch into main without a squash. The completion checklist includes checking the bootstrap forbidden services and the selected build-watch boundaries against the new pin.

p.CYCLE-ROLLBACK: **Rollback**: `cycle restart` - a `git reset --hard` of the cycle branch to the parent of the pin commit plus deletion of the state (confirmed by `--yes`).

p.MANDATORY-STOP-POINTS: The mandatory stop points: the toolchain advisory; manual conflicts; broken rules; patches to deleted files; a large design decision (stop, explain, offer the options).

canon.title: 5. The canonical commit set of a cycle and the trailers

p.CANONICAL-COMMIT-SET: The canonical set (it is not squashed on merge - otherwise the cost metric is lost): «bump pin»; «renames» (the artifacts carried over the renames); «regeneration» (machine-made - it may be thrown away and created anew); «deps/toolchain»; individual fixes, each with its own cause; «removal of the artifacts of files that disappeared» - always a separate commit with an explanation.

p.CYCLE-TRAILERS: The trailers: every commit of a cycle carries `Codkit-Cycle: <targetTag>`; fixes carry `Cause: <upstream SHA>` in addition. The codkit hook puts them there, CI checks them (without machine validation a trailer does not take root - the lesson of the references). The canonical messages produced under the hook are uniform, so that they are easy to search for.

p.ORCHESTRATOR-BUILT-LAST: The orchestrator is built **after** apply and extract are stable - a minimal version in the MVP (pin → apply → a report of the refusals → continue), the extension later. The tests of the orchestrator itself run on a fake fork tree (PROP-013 §2, §5): the git operations are real, the heavy parts are emulated.
